_about: Frozen from the v3.1 Sunnytime db.json (2026-09-28): every ingredient name it held, the flags v3.1 gave each name (from evidence lists), how often each name appeared, and the flag definitions. Rules v3.2 start from this map (scripts/sunnytime_db.py Engine).

hidden_uv_booster.l: UV booster not listed as a sunscreen active
hidden_uv_booster.w: Absorbs UV and can raise SPF while the label still reads 'mineral'.
hidden_uv_booster.s: FDA OTC sunscreen monograph (only listed actives may claim SPF); TinySafe label analysis. Bemotrizinol became an FDA-approved active in June 2026 — if it appears among inactives, it is still a hidden filter.

chemical_filter_in_inactives.l: Chemical UV filter listed among inactive ingredients
chemical_filter_in_inactives.w: A chemical filter used without being declared as an active.
chemical_filter_in_inactives.s: FDA OTC monograph; FDA absorption studies (JAMA 2019, 2020).

mi_mci.w: Among the most common contact allergens; the EU bans MI in leave-on cosmetics.
mi_mci.s: EU Regulation 2016/1198 (MI banned in leave-on); ACDS Allergen of the Year 2013.

formaldehyde_releaser.w: Slowly releases formaldehyde, a known contact allergen.
formaldehyde_releaser.s: ACDS Allergen of the Year 2015 (formaldehyde); EU Annex V labelling rule for releasers.

ipbc.w: The EU does not allow it in leave-on products for children under three.
ipbc.s: EU Cosmetics Regulation Annex V (iodopropynyl butylcarbamate entry) — verify current entry text.

retinoid.w: An adult skincare active; increases sun sensitivity.
retinoid.s: EU Regulation 2024/996 (vitamin A limits); AAD guidance on retinoids and sun.

adult_active.w: Exfoliants, brighteners and self-tanners aren't meant for baby skin.
adult_active.s: AAD; EU Annex III entries for arbutin and DHA.

spray_powder.w: Not recommended for children: it can be inhaled. The AAP advises against spraying sunscreen on a child's face.
spray_powder.s: AAP HealthyChildren.org, Sun Safety; FDA sunscreen guidance.

d4.w: Classified in the EU as toxic to reproduction; restricted in cosmetics.
d4.s: EU CLP classification (Repr. 2); EU REACH restriction; California AB 496.

talc_inhalable.l: Contains talc in a spray or powder
talc_inhalable.w: Talc's asbestos-contamination concern matters most when it can be inhaled; FDA proposed mandatory testing.
talc_inhalable.s: FDA proposed rule on asbestos testing in talc-containing cosmetics (Dec 2024).

triclosan.w: Antimicrobials the FDA removed from OTC antiseptic washes.
triclosan.s: FDA final rule on consumer antiseptic washes (2016).

formaldehyde.w: A known contact allergen and carcinogen.

no_preservative_water_base.w: Water-containing products need a preservative system or they can grow microbes.
no_preservative_water_base.s: FDA guidance on cosmetic microbiological safety; recall history for contaminated lotions.

phthalate.w: Endocrine-active plasticizers; restricted in the EU.

fragrance.w: Fragrance is the most common cause of cosmetic contact allergy.
fragrance.s: ACDS Allergen of the Year 2007 (fragrance); AAD; pediatric dermatology consensus (JDD 2020) recommends fragrance-free for infants.

eu_fragrance_allergen.w: On the EU list of substances that must be declared because they cause allergy in people.
eu_fragrance_allergen.s: EU Cosmetics Regulation Annex III; Regulation (EU) 2023/1545 (56 added; labelling from July 2026/2028).

essential_oil.w: Aromatic oils are frequent sensitizers on baby skin, even when 'fragrance' isn't on the label.
essential_oil.s: Contact Dermatitis literature on essential-oil allergy; SCCS opinions on lavender, tea tree.

asteraceae.l: Contains a plant from the ragweed (Asteraceae) family
asteraceae.w: Chamomile, calendula and arnica are among the most frequently reported plant sensitizers.
asteraceae.s: Contact Dermatitis reviews of Compositae/Asteraceae allergy; AAD.

oat.w: Oat sensitization is documented in children with eczema; also a food allergen.
oat.s: Boussault et al., Allergy 2007 (oat sensitization in atopic children).

tree_nut.l: Contains a tree-nut oil or extract
tree_nut.w: Major food allergen; refined oils carry low but not zero risk.
tree_nut.s: FALCPA; FARE guidance on refined oils.

soy.w: Major food allergen. Note: soy-derived tocopherol is not labelled as soy.

wheat.w: Major food allergen (hydrolyzed wheat protein has caused sensitization through skin).
wheat.s: FALCPA; Japanese HWP soap sensitization reports.

propolis_beeswax.w: Propolis is a documented contact allergen.

propylene_glycol.w: Irritant and allergen in some children.

drying_alcohol.w: Stings and dries; fatty alcohols (cetyl, stearyl) are not counted.

propyl_butyl_paraben.w: The EU bans these in leave-on products for the diaper area of children under three.

phenoxyethanol.w: Considered safe at ≤1%; some parents avoid it after France's 2012 advisory for under-threes (diaper area).
phenoxyethanol.s: CIR safety assessment; SCCS 2016; ANSM 2012 advisory.

methyl_ethyl_paraben.w: Considered safe by the SCCS; listed because parents ask.

ethoxylated.l: Contains PEG or other ethoxylated ingredients
ethoxylated.w: Manufacturing can leave trace 1,4-dioxane; New York limits it in personal care.

ethanolamines.w: Can form nitrosamines with certain preservatives.

petrolatum_mineral_oil.w: Cosmetic-grade is well tolerated; listed because it feels heavy and some parents prefer to avoid.

silicone.w: Texture and spread; not a safety flag.

iron_oxide_tint.w: Mineral pigments; listed because tint changes how it looks on skin.

synthetic_dye.w: Colour only; some dyes are reported sensitizers.

sodium_benzoate.w: Can cause non-allergic redness (contact urticaria) in sensitive skin.

botanical_count.w: Counted by botanical name; plants are the most common sensitizers on baby skin.
botanical_count.s: TinySafe label analysis; JDD 2020 pediatric consensus (sensitizer-free).

microplastic_polymer.w: May fall under the EU microplastics restriction; whether it does depends on the particle form and size, which a label does not show.

shea.w: Refined shea carries almost no allergenic protein; listed for families who avoid it.

coconut.w: Coconut allergy is rare; listed for families who avoid it.

d5_d6.w: Restricted in the EU for environmental persistence, not for skin safety.

talc.w: In a lotion or cream; listed because parents ask.

water_resistant.w: Film formers keep it on in water and make it harder to wash off.

chemical_filter_active.w: Absorbed through skin; FDA has asked for more safety data on these filters before confirming them as generally safe and effective.
chemical_filter_active.s: FDA proposed rule (2019) and proposed order (2021); Matta et al., JAMA 2019/2020.
